hazards.title: nf_sssp_csr_pred: an OUTPUT was shipped as an INPUT
hazards.hazard: The 8th argument is written as 4*(np-1) bytes of i32 predecessor data. The shipped wrapper hands it a caller buffer sized for a per-edge predicate byte array, so the write lands past the buffer and over the dist output that follows it.
hazards.evidence: MEASURED, ts/dist sha256 9594fe62: rc=0, dist=[0xFFFFFFFF x3] instead of [0,2,7].
hazards.consequence: Silently wrong distances with a success code. No trap, so errors.ts cannot catch it.

hazards.title: The exported artefact is one symbol behind the source
hazards.hazard: src/lib.rs declares 86 #[no_mangle] symbols; ts/dist/numfast_native.wasm exports 85. nf_pair_insert_i64 (lib.rs:2972) has no cfg gate and would be exported by a wasm build.
hazards.evidence: MEASURED: a fresh `cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --release` into a scratch CARGO_TARGET_DIR emits 86 function exports, 87 total, 21 of them i64 - and zero FuncType differences on the 85 it shares with the shipped one. The shipped sha256 matches BUILD.json, so the package is internally consistent and simply built from an older tree.
hazards.consequence: Every published count (85, 20, 'the other 68') is wrong by one, and the reproducibility guard the package relies on turns into a build FAILURE on a clean clone.

hazards.title: No bounds check exists anywhere at the FFI boundary
hazards.hazard: core::buffers::borrow / borrow_mut are raw slice::from_raw_parts{,_mut}. Every length, capacity and range is caller-enforced; the kernels do not validate them.
hazards.evidence: MEASURED: nf_mask_not(pA, -1, pOut) traps with RuntimeError: unreachable, because a negative i32 becomes a ~4.29e9-element slice. errors.ts documents the same class as '63 of the 85 kernels'.
hazards.consequence: A wrong length is undefined behaviour natively and a wasm trap (or silent corruption, if the address stays inside linear memory) on wasm32. There is no middle path.

hazards.title: 11 exports are dead on the wasm32 surface: they always trap
hazards.hazard: join.rs, join_i64.rs and groupby/hash_grouped.rs call std::thread::scope + scope.spawn with no #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")] fallback (only sssp.rs has one). wasm32-unknown-unknown cannot spawn, and Cargo.toml sets panic = "abort".
hazards.evidence: MEASURED traps (RuntimeError: unreachable) on nf_join_probe, nf_join_gather_i32, nf_join_fused_left_i32, nf_ghash_fp_i64, nf_ghash_occ_count. The other six share the identical call shape. nf_join_build (single-threaded) and nf_sssp_batch (wasm-gated) both return 0.
hazards.consequence: These symbols are reachable through callRaw and will trap on every non-empty call. Nothing in the source or the wasm doc comments says so - and the source comments actually claim the opposite ('no wasm export', 'Native-only').

hazards.title: Pointer-to-pointer crosses the ABI as one i32
hazards.hazard: nf_rowwise_kway_time_argmin_gather takes *const *const i32 and *const *const f32. In wasm these are single i32s: the ADDRESS of an offset array. A wrapper that writes lane data there, or that passes the offset array itself, is wrong in a way no type check will catch.
hazards.evidence: census + FuncType (two i32 params, no i64/f32 at those positions)
hazards.consequence: The only exported pointer-to-pointer. It is documented in ts/abi.ts, but no length accompanies it.

hazards.title: Three symbols derive their row count from a data value
hazards.hazard: nf_ghash_pins_i64 takes n = starts[p]; nf_ghash_occ_count takes m = toff[p]; nf_ghash_occ_fill takes m = toff[p] and nocc = ostart[p]. There is no n or m parameter at all.
hazards.evidence: census (length_expression column: the borrow() length is a dereference of a caller lane)
hazards.consequence: Reading these as (buffer, count) pairs - the natural reading from the name - is exactly the convention error that left 69 kernels unwrapped. Every other *_i64/_i32 symbol does take a count.

hazards.title: -1 and -2 are overloaded: they do not mean 'you passed null'
hazards.hazard: nf_group_owner_2i32_1f64 returns -1 for a null pointer AND for lo > hi / hi > g. nf_unique_dict_utf8 returns -1 for a null pointer AND for every geometry rejection (offs_len != n+1, n > i32::MAX, data_len > i32::MAX, and a bad-offset failure from the kernel). nf_rng_sample_no_replace returns -2 for null AND for k > n.
hazards.consequence: A wrapper that renders -1 as 'null pointer' will state a falsehood about a range error. errors.ts resolves codes through a per-symbol table precisely to avoid this, but the table has to carry the second meaning or it is worse than a bare number.

hazards.title: Argument order does not follow a pointer-then-its-length convention
hazards.hazard: Counter-examples that break the naive reading: nf_pack_sum_count_i32/f64 put the scalar m2 BEFORE n; nf_select_scatter_* take (src, mask, n, out) so the output is last while two inputs precede n; nf_segment_reduce_* take (values, n, bounds, m, op, out); nf_pattern_encode interleaves (ptr, len) pairs but ends with two 1-lane scalar-out pointers; nf_router_route puts the vertex count n FIRST, before every pointer.
hazards.evidence: MEASURED over the whole census: 346 pointer parameters across 86 symbols; only 35 of them (10%) are immediately preceded by the scalar that determines their length. All 86 symbols have at least one pointer whose sizing scalar is somewhere else in the argument list. Worst offenders: nf_rowwise_min4_argmin_gather and nf_rowwise_min4_time_argmin_gather (10 of 12 pointers non-adjacent), nf_join_fused_left_i32 (9 of 13), nf_ghash_pins_i64 and nf_group_owner_2i32_1f64 (8 each).
hazards.consequence: This is the measured reason a wrapper written from a signature alone is a guess, and why 69 kernels were left unwrapped: 'pointer then its length' is true for one pointer in ten.

hazards.title: Source comments contradict the build for seven kernel families
hazards.hazard: 'no wasm export', 'Native-only', 'no WASM export (native CPU research surface)' appear above nf_join_build/probe/gather/fused_*, nf_join_build_i64/probe_i64, nf_sort_perm_*, nf_unique_inverse_*, nf_unique_dict_utf8, nf_segment_*, nf_adjacency_*, nf_cost_*, nf_ghash_*, nf_rowwise_*, nf_bounded_select_2i32, nf_sssp_*, nf_pair_insert_i64 - all of which ARE exported by the shipped artefact. nf_pair_insert_i64 is the one symbol where the comment is accidentally right.
hazards.evidence: wasm export list of ts/dist/numfast_native.wasm vs the source comments
hazards.consequence: A reader deciding what is reachable from these comments reaches the opposite of the truth for 15 symbols, and the one place a reader would look to confirm nf_pair_insert_i64's status is the comment that is right for the wrong reason.
